predecessors.name: Oirat Confederation (17th century)
predecessors.text: the Oirat core in Dzungaria that Cliopatria draws as the Oirat Confederation (365,737 km2 in 1634)

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Dzungaria, the Ili country and the Tarim Basin: 'From 1755 to 1758, Qing dynasty took advantage of a Dzungar civil war to conquer Dzungaria'; 'The Tarim Basin was pacified in 1759'; without Hami…

ledger.x: 1634: Erdeni Batur founds the Dzungar Khanate on the upper Emil River.
1643: Erdeni Batur's army enters Kazakh lands.
1658: the Kazakh frontier is fixed.
1658: eastern Semirechye passes to the Dzungars.
1679: Galdan takes Turpan and Hami.
1680: the Dzungars conquer the Tarim Basin.
1684: the Syr Darya cities fall to Galdan.
1687: Tauke Khan drives Galdan out.
August 1688: Galdan conquers Khalkha Mongolia.
September 1690: the Qing meet Galdan at Ulan Butung.
1696: Hami leaves the Dzungar state.
June 1696: Galdan is routed at Zuunmod.
1696: Outer Mongolia goes to the Qing.
August 1717: the Dzungars enter Tibet.
December 1717: Lha-bzang Khan dies at the Potala.
December 1717: the Dzungars hold Central Tibet.
1720: the Qing drive the Dzungars out of Tibet.
1723: the Dzungars take the Syr Darya cities.
1731: the Qing invade, the Dzungars win at Khoton Lake.
1739: the Khalkha-Dzungar boundary is agreed.
1745: the Dzungar hold on Jetisu and Tashkent ends.
Spring 1755: the Qing army enters the Dzungar lands.
1757: the last resistance ends.
1757: the Dzungar hold on the Tarim Basin ends.
1757: Dzungaria goes to the Qing.
1757: the Dzungar Khanate is no more.

wars.name: Kazakh-Dzungar Wars
wars.outcome: Dzungar gains in Semirechye (1658) and on the Syr Darya (1684-87, 1723-1745); the Kazakhs won at Bulanty (1726) and in 1727-1730; the last war ended in May 1741, with Dzungar hostages from the Middle Jus in 1742.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of the Tarim Basin
wars.outcome: Galdan conquers Kashgar and Yarkant (1680), installs a client and holds the Tarim Basin to 1757.

wars.name: Khoshut-Dzungar war (Galdan against Ochirtu)
wars.outcome: Galdan defeats Chechen Tayiji near Sayram Lake (1676) and Ochirtu (1677 on the Dzungar page, 1678 on the Galdan page); Ochirtu flees to Kokonor and Galdan dominates the Oirats.

wars.name: First Dzungar-Qing War
wars.outcome: Galdan wins at Olgoi Nor (3 Aug 1688), meets the Qing at Ulan Butung (Sept 1690), is routed at Zuunmod (12 June 1696) and dies in 1697; Outer Mongolia passes to the Qing.

wars.name: Dzungar conquest of Tibet
wars.outcome: Tsewang Rabtan's army enters Tibet (25 Aug 1717), kills Lha-bzang Khan (2 Dec 1717), destroys a Qing relief force at the Salween River (1718) and is expelled by the Qing in 1720.

wars.name: Third Dzungar-Qing War
wars.outcome: Dzungar victory at Khoton Lake (1731), Khalkha victory at Erdene Zuu (1732); peace and a fixed boundary in 1739.

wars.name: Dzungar-Kokand clashes
wars.outcome: 'The Dzungars invaded Kokand in 1742 and 1745 and were repelled'; no frontier moved.

wars.name: Qing conquest of Dzungaria
wars.outcome: Qing victory: the khanate destroyed in 1755, Amursana's revolt and the Dzungar genocide 1755-1758, the Tarim Basin pacified in 1759.

certainty.note: Steppe and oasis frontiers; the Kazakh border 'from the Ayagoz River to the Talas River' (1658) is described by its rivers only.
The Khalkha-Dzungar boundary is agreed in 1739 and so firmer there; every other frontier stays soft.
